subject.title: media: agent-scoped roots expose sibling sandbox files

question: Should media authorization remove the shared stateDir/sandboxes parent and require callers to provide the exact active agent or session sandbox root?
rationale: The isolation requirement is clear, but maintainers must confirm which runtime context owns the canonical active sandbox identity so the fix closes sibling access without breaking legitimate sandbox-generated attachments.

options.title: Thread the exact active sandbox
options.body: Remove the shared parent from defaults and pass only the active agent/session sandbox root through the relevant media call paths, preserving legitimate scoped access.

options.title: Disallow sandbox host paths
options.body: Remove sandbox directories from host-media roots entirely and require sandbox-specific transfer or hydration APIs for every sandbox artifact.

options.title: Retain shared sandbox access
options.body: Keep the broad parent allowlist and explicitly accept that agent-scoped media paths can authorize sibling sandbox files.

recommendation.title: Thread the exact active sandbox
recommendation.body: Remove the shared parent from defaults and pass only the active agent/session sandbox root through the relevant media call paths, preserving legitimate scoped access.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing candidate from merged media-security and path-validation history, while the final boundary choice spans several caller surfaces.
